what_happened: The design job "Design continuous drain-owned landing to remove post-verifier wait" was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier found one major problem and no blockers. The design note (docs/design/continuous-landing.md, sections 1, 2, 4 and Rollback) describes today's landing without having read the drain code. The drain already rebases, re-checks and merges inside one locked slot. The real wait comes from the Landing::Waiting transfer after a check poll of about 10 minutes. The note never names that transfer or the simpler fix. No acceptance criteria or failed checks were listed as unmet.
cause: Design jobs have no required step that inventories how the current system actually works before the doc proposes a change. For a redesign of an existing flow, nothing makes the writer read the code path being redesigned, state the current behaviour with file and function references, and name the measured cause of the problem. The reading and planning stages accept a request's framing ("drain-owned landing") as a description of the present state. A doc written from that framing looks complete. Only the verifier, reading the code at the end, notices that the premise is wrong and a simpler fix exists. This is the third case of the same gap.
prevention: Add a mandatory "current state" step to every design job, enforced in the plan and by a code check on the doc. The doc must contain a section "Current behaviour" that cites the existing code (file and function or type names, for example Landing::Waiting) and the relevant recorded decisions. A code check must confirm that each cited path and symbol resolves in the snapshot. The planner must reject a design plan that has no such inventory. The doc must also name the measured cause of the problem it addresses and compare its proposal with the smallest alternative fix. With that, a design that ignores the existing transfer, or rebuilds something that exists, fails before the final verdict.
proposed_request: Redo the design note docs/design/continuous-landing.md on removing the wait between the verifier's pass and the merge. Start by reading the drain and landing code. In a section "Current behaviour", describe how landing works today, citing the files and functions or types involved. Include that the drain already rebases, re-checks and merges within one locked slot, and that the wait comes from the Landing::Waiting transfer after a check poll of about 10 minutes. State the measured cause of the wait, with the timings you used. Then compare at least two options: the smallest change that removes or shortens the transfer, and the larger drain-owned continuous landing. Recommend one, and give its rollback, its effect on parallel runs (max_concurrency > 1), and the tests that would show it works. Every claim about current behaviour must match the code in the snapshot. Change only the design note and, if needed, the changelog. Do not change code.
